title: `prune --apply` acts on this machine only, from a live snapshot, with `git branch -d` / `worktree remove` and no force flags, after confirmation; the MCP surface is read-only
context: Deleting somebody's unmerged work is the one irreversible action this feature could take, and stored records (a cloned .hunch/, a shared overlay) are attacker-controllable input.
decision: The prune plan for this machine is computed from a snapshot taken moments ago, never from a stored record; other machines' commands are printed from their stored records and never executed here. Rules: proven merged, not the default branch, worktree clean, unlocked, present, not the main worktree. Execution is fixed-argv git with `--`, `-d` not `-D`, `worktree remove` without `--force` (git re-checks clean/merged as a second line of defense), after an interactive confirmation or an explicit --yes off a terminal; remotes are never touched. `hunch_workspaces` has no write or prune surface. A record collision in the other memory home is reported with the `forget` remedy, never thrown out of an apply.
consequences: A forged 'merged' record cannot cause a delete (tested end to end).
Cross-machine cleanup is a human running printed commands on that machine, by design.
alternatives_rejected: An MCP prune/write tool — an agent could act unattended on what a record claims.
Acting on stored verdicts (`--apply` from memory) — memory is display-only; a record carries no authority.
Deleting remote branches or executing on another machine — irreversible and out of this machine's jurisdiction.
`-D` / `--force` when git refuses — git's refusal is the safety net, not an obstacle.
